To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

endobronchial ultrasonography-guided transbronchial lung biopsy (EBUS-TBLB) is a safe and reliable procedure for the diagnosis of peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) and that EBUS is superior to CT-guided transthoracic needle biopsy (CT-TNB) in the diagnosis of small-sized PPLs (≤ 20mm in diameter).

the use of endobronchial ultrasonography (EBUS)-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (TBNA) for the diagnosis of peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) is a safe and effective procedure with a high diagnostic accuracy.

(1) the sensitivity of EBUS-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (TBNA) for mediastinal and hilar lymph node sampling was 92% in 200 consecutive patients, (2) the sensitivity for mediastinal lymph node sampling was higher than that of conventional TBNA, and (3) EBUS-guided TBNA was a safe procedure.
